_meta.description: Afterglow turns an iPhone and a printed viewer into a real headset: 6DoF passthrough, hand tracking, spatial photos, 360 panoramas, a WebXR browser and games in your own room. Free and open source.
a-360-photo-all.b89a2b: A 360 photo all around you, with its filmstrip
a-360-photo-as.4109a2: A 360 photo as the surroundings, with its filmstrip
a-native-start-page.de79a8: A native start page, a keyboard you can type on through the lens, and a quiet exit: double-tap the viewer.
a-short-bill-of.88b1a2: A short bill of materials: two lenses and a strap.
a-webxr-browser-your.54beee: A WebXR browser your hands reach into
afterglow-is-tuned-for.13f6bc: Afterglow is tuned for a viewer you print yourself: a shell sized to the iPhone 18 Pro Max, a lens tray, and a cover that leaves the cameras clear so passthrough and hand tracking can see.
afterglow-presents-itself-to.208c6c: Afterglow presents itself to pages as a headset with hand tracking. Sessions run with ultra-wide passthrough and head rotation; the page gets your hands as input sources.
afterglow-runs-on-the.c14d2d: Afterglow runs on the phone. Your photos, your room and your hands never leave it. The whole app is open source, so you can read exactly what it does.
albums-a-filmstrip-a.bbdb87: Albums, a filmstrip, a scrub bar, and projection you can switch when a file lies about what it is.
an-apple-watch-can.74863e: An Apple Watch can also act as a controller: wrist taps and the crown, over a thin connection to the phone.
arkit-gives-afterglow-six.769f93: ARKit gives Afterglow six degrees of freedom, so you can lean in, step round and look behind. The cameras pass your room through, and glass windows float in it with a launcher and a dock at your feet.
browse-flat-pages-in.4fa6a1: Browse flat pages in a floating window, then enter immersive WebXR sessions with your hands as the controllers. Pages get head pose, hand joints and pinch events, the way a headset would give them.
cardboard-showed-a-phone.f91bd2: Cardboard showed a phone could be a headset. Afterglow finishes the thought: real head tracking, your hands, your room, and an interface you can actually read through a lens.
coaster-a-new-course.628ac5: Coaster: a new course every ride
do-i-need-the.145ff6: Do I need the printed viewer?
every-game-ends-with.d35189: Every game ends with a summary
files-your-folders-with.3fe3e7: Files: your folders, with a search typed on the keyboard
for-the-headset-experience.aaf298: For the headset experience, yes, or any Cardboard-style viewer with an open front for the cameras. Without one, phone view shows a single eye and lets you tap the screen to select what the centre cursor is on.
for-tracks-in-your.2d2c75: For tracks in your own library it analyses the audio on the phone. For Apple Music songs it looks the tempo up by title and artist, using audiometa.io, and tells you which source it used. If neither knows the song, you set the tempo yourself.
fork-it-build-it.110ca5: Fork it, build it, change it. The source, the viewer files and the test harness are all in the repository.
free-and-open-source.bef778: Free and open source (Apache-2.0). Built for the iPhone 18 Pro Max.
get-it-on-the.c04ddf: Get it on the App Store
glow-garden-plants-grow.6452fe: Glow garden: plants grow where you point
hand-tracking-runs-on.ab40fe: Hand tracking runs on the Neural Engine. Pinch to select, grab to move, point to aim. No controller, nothing to charge.
is-it-on-the.33fbe9: Is it on the App Store?
it-is-built-and.c5a125: It is built and tested on the iPhone 18 Pro Max, with the printed viewer sized to it. Other recent Pro iPhones with LiDAR should work, but the viewer and the lens geometry are tuned for the 18 Pro Max.
make-a-door-for.57ddc5: Make a door for your iPhone
mini-golf-eighteen-holes.9f5d6e: Mini golf: eighteen holes at your feet
one-of-twenty-four.7b95f4: One of twenty-four places to be
orbital-pong-your-palms.9bfd08: Orbital pong: your palms are the paddles
paint-in-the-air.dfd4de: Paint in the air with glowing tubes. Putt eighteen holes of mini golf at your feet. Ride a coaster on a course that is new every time. Shoot blobs, vacuum the floor, wake a toy box, open a portal. Stack a tower on your real table, grow a glowing garden, keep a ball in orbit with your palms, and drive a neon road by looking where you want to go.
pick-a-photosphere-and.7adf61: Pick a photosphere and the room is gone: a mountain lake, a desert at dusk, a city at night. Bring your own 360 photos and they sit alongside the bundled ones.
places-are-stills-with.a4efcc: Places are stills, with no server behind them. Everything renders on the phone.
places-twenty-four-photospheres.b25876: Places: twenty-four photospheres to be in
portal-step-through-to.21a62f: Portal: step through to another world
print-it-three-parts.06d4db: Print it. Three parts, no electronics.
ready-to-print-on.86a52a: Ready to print on MakerWorld, with OpenSCAD source in the repository.
rendered-by-the-app.6ad965: Rendered by the app itself in the iPhone Simulator, which has no camera, so its synthwave surroundings stand in for your room. On a phone these float in your real room, in stereo.
rhythm-plays-to-real.e4831f: Rhythm plays to real music. Afterglow measures the tempo of your own tracks, and for songs from Apple Music it looks the beat up so the game lands on it.
song-tempo-data-by.6d2e1c: Song tempo data by audiometa.io. Head and hand tracking are Apple's ARKit and Vision frameworks. The bundled photospheres are the author's own.
song-tempo-data-for.11e0b8: Song tempo data for the rhythm game is provided by audiometa.io.
spatial-photos-and-videos.9633de: Spatial photos and videos from an iPhone or Vision Pro play back in stereo. Panoramas wrap round you. 360 photos become the room itself, found automatically across your whole library.
tap-the-viewer-to.61f3c0: Tap the viewer to select. Double-tap to leave an immersive session.
the-browser-with-its.340dc9: The browser, with its tabs and address bar
the-browser-with-its.393483: The browser, with its tabs and text-size controls
the-interface-and-every.18f415: The interface and every experience, from where you stand. Each picture is one eye without the lens warp, unless it says through the lenses.
the-launcher-from-inside.42c60d: The launcher, from inside the viewer
there-are-no-accounts.2632fb: There are no accounts and no analytics. The only network calls are the ones you make: the pages you browse, and a tempo lookup for a song you chose. A web page gets your hand positions only if you allow it, site by site.
tower-stack-slabs-on.512ec5: Tower: stack slabs on a real table
toys-a-box-that.5923ce: Toys: a box that comes alive
twelve-games-in-your.d44da0: Twelve games in your own room
webxr-ar-a-page.da393f: WebXR AR: a page placing a reticle on your floor
webxr-vr-through-the.7d47ec: WebXR VR, through the lenses, with Exit VR at your feet
what-about-webxr-sites.13fabc: What about WebXR sites that need a headset?
what-the-phone-s.f9f185: What the phone's screen really shows
where-does-the-rhythm.95877b: Where does the rhythm game get its tempo?
which-phones-does-it.62d321: Which phones does it run on?
windows-hang-where-you.207b19: Windows hang where you leave them. Captured without a camera, so synthwave stands in for your room.
windows-side-by-side.aa4c18: Windows side by side, where you put them
windows-that-stay-where.5a5a7e: Windows that stay where you put them
yes-as-afterglow-xr.36c5bb: Yes, as Afterglow XR, free. It is also open source, so you can build it yourself and put it on your own iPhone with Xcode.
your-photos-and-videos.ebe17d: Your photos and videos in 3D. Panoramas and 360 photos all around you. A WebXR browser your hands can reach into. Games in your own room. All on the iPhone in your pocket and a viewer you print.
